about:
The program's structure enables students to obtain an M.A. degree within 1 year (3 semesters) in the non-thesis track - Fall, Spring and Summer. Students in the non-thesis track are required to complete a total of 36 hours of study. Courses include seminars, mandatory and elective courses, and field projects. Mandatory courses - 12 hours | Elective courses - 10 hours | Two seminars of 6-7 hours in total (one mandatory and one elective) | Research and Project Workshop - 4 hours| Fieldwork - 4 hours.
All mandatory courses during the first two semesters will be concentrated in a single weekday – Monday from morning to evening. Electives and opportunities for internships will be offered through the rest of the week. Electives can be chosen from dedicated courses that will be offered by the program, courses in other international programs in the university, or from courses in other faculties such as engineering, exact or life sciences contingent on relevance to development and must be approved by the program head.
Example:
Sustainability and Public Policy (the department of Public Policy)
Why Anthropology? (the department of Sociology and Anthropology)
Courses from the international English programs - Conflict Resolution, Crisis management, Climate Change, etc.
During the semester break (February) the students continue their activity and learning. For example, taking a field trip and visit to relevant sites in Israel, where they will be able to witness first-hand the deployment of innovative technologies and interventions related to sustainable development. Or participating in an intensive workshop in human and sustainable development.
In the third (summer) semester, students will be required to apply their learnings in a practical manner through intensive fieldwork that will be conducted in teams in sites in Israel or in other countries in Asia or Africa where Tel Aviv University is working with local partners from academia, civil society and industry.
Students in the non-thesis track are required to prepare a final written assignment (project evaluation) based on their fieldwork.The final grade in the standard track consists of class grades (90%) and the grade of the final project assignment (10%).
Students are expected to attend all classes.
Deadlines for submitting course / workshop completion papers:
Deadlines for submission the paper of the course/seminar:
Submission of final papers for the course taught in the fall semester – Sunday, March 8, 2026;
Submission of final papers for the course taught in the spring semester - Sunday, August 16, 2026;
Submission of final papers for the course taught in the summer semester - Up to 6 weeks from the end of the semester (from September 18, 2026).
Deadlines for submission seminars' works:
Fall semester - Sunday, April 19, 2026;
Spring semester and two semester courses - Thursday, September 17, 2026;
Summer semester - Sunday, November 1, 2026.
Registration to classes is done via the program office – sustaindev@tauex.tau.ac.il. All students are registered by the program coordinator to all mandatory courses. Students will let the program office know, by email, what are the elective courses and seminars they chose. In all communication to sustaindev@tauex.tau.ac.il, students must include their student id ≠.

sections.name: Fieldwork
sections.note:
SUMMER SEMESTER
The challenges of sustainable development cannot be understood through classroom teaching alone. It can be gradually developed by students only through an intensive, direct experience that lies in an in-depth understanding and practical work.
The program, therefore, integrates a strong component of experiential learning in its curriculum that includes prolonged immersion in field sites, either in Israel or in sites in developing countries, where students engage in applied research and fieldwork. Students in the program form bridges between technology providers (including in Israel) and the realities of low-income communities by designing, adapting, and field-testing promising solutions that combine innovative technologies and business models.
Students are encouraged to conduct their fieldwork within existing sites where TAU faculties are working with local academic, government, NGO, and industry partners. In particular, projects run by the Nitsan Lab at TAU (nitsanlab.org) offer ample opportunities for students to get involved and try out their ideas in real settings in several dedicated sites in India and Africa.
